summary: Yu-Chen Tsui specializes in Buddhist studies. Tsui completed a master's at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü, pursued doctoral studies supervised by Natasha Heller (attested 2018), and also studied under the traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-kwan Ng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Ng studied under Zongsan Mou at CUHK (~1968–1974) and earned a Ph.D. at McMaster University (~1980–1985) under Yün-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara, later holding posts at HKBU (1988) and NCU (~1999–2011).

Yu-min Lee is a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington. Lee later served as Professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002) and taught Pei-jung Wu.
Yuan Ren works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ren earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Gongga Rinpoche. Guo held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and served as a researcher at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism.

Yuanying (1878–1953) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under teachers including Zeng Xi, Miaolian, Yekai, and Bazhi Toutuo. He served as abbot at Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples and held leadership posts in the Buddhist Association of China.

Yudru Tsomu is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who earned a PhD at Harvard University under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and advisors Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn. Tsomu taught Hoong Teik Toh and Cameron David Warner.

Yuen Ren Chao (1892–1982) was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Cornell (~1910–1914) and Harvard (~1915–1918). He held academic posts at Cornell (~1919–1920), Harvard (~1921–1924), Tsinghua University (~1925–1929), and UC Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served there as a teacher.

Yuguang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University (~1965–1974) and later served as its president (~2011–2015).

Yui Chi Lau (1914–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Ying-Kuang Chu. Lau founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society and taught Shek-Wing Tam.

Yui Suzuki specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. Suzuki studied at UCLA under doctoral supervisors William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Kyoto University and studied in India, the UK, and Austria. He held professorships at Kyoto University (1956–1988), Bukkyo University, and Soka University.
Yuichi Shionoya (1932–2015) was a philosopher who studied at Nagoya University (~1950–1953) and Hitotsubashi University (~1953–1958). He held a post at Nagoya University (~1964–1970).

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, earning a doctorate from Bukkyo University, where he taught from 1961 to 1997. He later served as president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College and Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, and held posts at Shōjōke-in and Chion-in.

Yujiro Motora (1858–1912) was a philosopher who studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1888–1912) and Tokyo University of Education (~1888–1900), and taught Daijō Tokiwa.

Yujun Endo (1939–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who taught Kokan Fujita and Ryuichi Abe. Endo held faculty positions at Taisho University (attested 1991, 2014) and served as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who held part-time lecturer positions at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (both attested 2015).

Yukari Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Kimura completed doctoral studies under Kenyu Mitomo and is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University (attested 2026).
